name: electron

phase_0.boundary_condition: The asymptotic detection surface — a calorimeter or tracking volume that irreversibly records the electron's passage and terminates its coherent propagation.

⊢.justification: The unexcited electron field before any quantum number is assigned; the vacuum sector with zero fermion number.

⊣.justification: The hermetic detector surface that closes the system — once the electron deposits energy here, its coherent quantum evolution ends and the measurement record is fixed.

≻.justification: Unitary time evolution of the electron wavepacket between interactions; the forward morphism of free Dirac propagation.

≺.justification: The CPT-conjugate process — positron propagation backward in time — which clears the register while preserving the chirality frame structure.

⋈.justification: Sequential chaining of interaction vertices (photon emission, weak boson exchange, Higgs coupling) along the electron's worldline.

⊙.justification: The electron's identity as an indistinguishable quantum excitation — every electron is every other electron; the field quantum recognizes itself.

∈.justification: The electron field splits into left-handed (weak-isospin doublet) and right-handed (weak-isospin singlet) components — a genuine structural fork with different gauge couplings on each arm.

∋.justification: The Higgs Yukawa coupling rejoins the chiral arms into a massive Dirac fermion; the arms carry different weak charges and rejoin to a B-state (both chiralities present in the mass eigenstate).

⊤.justification: The left-handed arm affirmatively couples to W bosons — constructive truth of weak interaction participation.

⊥.justification: The right-handed arm has no charged-current coupling — constructive falsity of W-vertex participation, only Z/photon.

⊞.justification: The Z2 fermion-parity protection holds both particle and antiparticle sectors simultaneously — a live contradiction (B-state) that cannot be resolved without pair creation.

⊡.justification: A silicon pixel or drift-tube hit — an append-only, irreversible measurement record that freezes the electron's position and momentum at that spacetime point.

phase_2.failure_reason: Tri-ancestral reconnection over a transformed object — closes

phase_3.void_description: Unexcited electron field — zero fermion number, no quantum numbers assigned, the vacuum sector before pair creation.
phase_3.true_description: Left-handed electron component — affirmatively participates in charged-current weak interaction, carries weak isospin T3 = -1/2.
phase_3.false_description: Right-handed electron component — constructively lacks charged-current coupling, carries weak isospin T3 = 0.
phase_3.both_description: Massive Dirac electron — both chiralities simultaneously present, fermion parity Z2-protected, the physical electron observed in nature with definite mass and charge.

steps.domain_action: Initialize the electron field void — zero fermion number, no quantum numbers, the vacuum sector before any excitation.
The field quantum recognizes itself — every electron excitation is identical, establishing the self-referential identity of the fermion field.
Chirality bifurcation — the massless field splits into left-handed (weak doublet) and right-handed (weak singlet) arms, a genuine structural fork with different gauge representations.
Left arm — weak charged current vertex. The left-handed electron affirmatively couples to W bosons (EVALT deposits T), enabling beta decay and neutrino interactions.
Left arm — propagation between weak vertices. Unitary Dirac evolution of the left-handed component through spacetime.
Left arm — sequential composition of weak vertices. Chains W-emission/absorption events along the worldline.
Right arm — no charged current. The right-handed electron constructively lacks W coupling (EVALF deposits F), only neutral current and electromagnetic interactions.
Right arm — propagation between electromagnetic vertices. Unitary evolution of the right-handed component.
Right arm — sequential composition of photon vertices. Chains photon emission/absorption (Compton, bremsstrahlung) along the worldline.

Fermion parity protection — the Z2 topological invariant holds both particle and antiparticle sectors simultaneously (B-state), a live contradiction that cannot be resolved without crossing the pair-creation threshold.

Dirac mass recombination — the Higgs Yukawa coupling rejoins the chiral arms into a massive Dirac fermion. The arms carry different weak charges and fuse to B (both chiralities present), not to the massless input.
Massive electron propagation — unitary evolution of the physical electron with mass 0.511 MeV, charge -1, definite chirality mixing.
Electromagnetic vertex chain — sequential photon couplings (ionization, bremsstrahlung, pair production) along the massive electron's track.
⋈: High-fidelity vertex — each QED vertex enforces gauge symmetry and momentum conservation with near-deterministic precision (𐑐 fidelity).
≺: Signed polarity — the electron's negative charge establishes a single donating pole for electromagnetic interaction, no complementary accepting pole.
≻: Soft association — electromagnetic and weak interactions are reversible, non-covalent, mediated by gauge boson exchange without permanent structural transformation.
∈: Local interaction — each vertex is confined to a single spacetime point, no intrinsic correlation propagation beyond the immediate event (𐑲 granularity).
∋: Disjunctive partner selection — any single gauge boson (photon, W, Z, Higgs) suffices for a vertex; no simultaneous multi-partner conjunction required (𐑜 stoichiometry).
⊤: Low kinetic barrier — the free electron explores its quantum configuration space freely, reversible unitary evolution unless externally perturbed (𐑘 character).
⊙: Subcritical regime — the free electron exhibits no scale-free correlations or critical threshold behavior (𐑢 phase).
⊥: Persistent chirality — structurally enforced left/right components that do not thermally interconvert, maintaining distinct weak couplings across multiple axes (𐑖 chirality).
⊞: Pairwise stoichiometry — fundamental 1:1 participation ratio in every vertex (𐑙 stoichiometry).
⊡: Z2 protection — fermion parity conservation requires topological boundary crossing (pair creation/annihilation) to change the electron's state (𐑴 protection).
First track hit — a silicon pixel records the electron's position and momentum irreversibly, freezing the quantum state into a classical measurement record.
Hit composition — sequential chaining of detector hits forms the reconstructed track, each hit a CLINK in the measurement chain.
Second track hit — another irreversible record, appended to the track, further constraining the electron's trajectory.
Hit composition — continued chaining of measurement records.
Calorimeter energy deposit — the final irreversible record where the electron's energy is fully absorbed and the coherent propagation terminates.
Detection boundary closure — the hermetic detector surface closes the system; the electron's quantum evolution ends, the measurement record is complete and fixed.
Self-reference at termination — the detected electron identifies itself as the same quantum excitation that began at VINIT, closing the loop.

phase_5.compiler_frontend: The Standard Model Lagrangian — translates gauge symmetries (SU(3)×SU(2)×U(1)) and Yukawa couplings into vertex rules and propagation kernels.
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: Gauge boson exchange — photons, W/Z bosons, and Higgs mediate communication between the electron field and other sectors; the vertex is the message-passing primitive.
phase_5.memory_mechanism: Quantum field state — the Fock space of the electron field stores occupation numbers, momenta, and spins; measurement records (IFIX) write to classical detector memory.
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: Hamiltonian time evolution — the Dirac Hamiltonian orders operations along the worldline; vertices occur at interaction times dictated by coupling constants and phase space.
phase_5.alfs_store: The Particle Data Group (PDG) review — the canonical reference for electron mass, charge, magnetic moment, and coupling constants; the bootstrap store for this domain's numerical parameters.

phase_6.cycle_cost: One quantum of action (ℏ) per vertex — each interaction vertex consumes a unit of phase-space volume; measurement (IFIX) exports entropy to the detector's thermal bath.
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: Coherent quantum superposition — the electron wavepacket evolves unitarily, von Neumann entropy zero, information fully encoded in the field state.
phase_6.post_cycle_state: Classical measurement record — the track hits and calorimeter deposit are irreversible, increasing detector entropy by k_B ln(2) per bit recorded; the quantum coherence is lost.
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — the fundamental vertex operations are unitary and entropy-conserving; only the terminal IFIX/TANCH sequence exports entropy to the macroscopic detector, balancing the quantum information gain.

≺=𐑿: The electron carries a signed negative charge (−1), establishing a single donating pole for electromagnetic interaction without a complementary accepting pole on the same particle.
⋈=𐑐: The electron's fundamental interactions (e.g., photon emission/absorption, weak vertex) are governed by precise gauge symmetries and conservation laws, enforcing near-deterministic, geometry-constrained vertices with effectively infinite fidelity per quantum event.

∈=𐑲: The electron's fundamental interactions (e.g., vertex with a photon) are local quantum events confined to a single spacetime point, with no intrinsic propagation of correlation to neighboring units beyond the immediate vertex.
∋=𐑜: The electron engages in fundamental pairwise interactions (e.g., with a photon, W/Z boson, or Higgs) where any single partner from the available gauge boson set suffices for a vertex, without requiring simultaneous multi-partner conjunction.
